title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 50 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and allies & theaters.

stories.h: IonQ to Buy Zero Trust Firm Elisity in Deal Worth Up to $1.3B
stories.what: The Elisity purchase will pair microsegmentation with IonQ’s post-quantum cryptography as federal PQC migration deadlines approach.
stories.you: State hackers are still inside critical networks, which keeps defensive and offensive cyber in demand.

stories.h: General Atomics Receives $248M Coast Guard Order for MQ-9B Aircraft
stories.what: The MQ-9B SkyGuardian will support maritime surveillance, search and rescue, border protection, and other operational missions.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: Air Books $200M DOW Contract for Army NGC2 Software Delivery
stories.what: Air has secured a potential five-year, $200 million DOW contract to support Army NGC2 with its AI-native readiness software.
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

stories.h: NASA Issues Final RFP for Commercial Space Stations in LEO After ISS Retirement
stories.what: NASA expects to award commercial LEO destination contracts on April 15, 2027, with proposals due Dec. 8.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: North Korea unveils copy of Canadian armored vehicle
stories.what: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has opened a new national defense museum packed with the country’s missiles, rocket launchers and drones, and among the exhibits is a previously unseen 4 4 armored vehicle that closely resembles the Canadian-made Roshel Senator…
stories.you: Ground robots are moving from demos to real orders, starting with logistics and dangerous jobs.

watch.why: Around November 3. Whether US commercial growth keeps outpacing government revenue.

idea.h: GPS-denied navigation module ('Intel Inside' for drones)
idea.why: A small vision, inertial and terminal-guidance board any airframe maker can integrate; later, quantum-ready. Jamming is everywhere; most vendors can't build autonomy in-house. As airframes become commodities, the margin sits in components like this.
